🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-11-12 23:00 → 2026-11-13 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **Proving stack refactor proposed** — soundness hardening and a performance overhaul arrived together in one reviewable change for the group's proving work. [zkIE PR #47](https://github.com/trustless-ai/zkIE/pull/47)

> **Evaluation semantics sharpened** — the ERC-8183 thread pinned down the difference between a check that leaves no record and a dedicated record for checks that could not run. [ERC-8183 post 457](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8183-agentic-commerce/27902/457)

> **Provable inference lead surfaced** — a paper on an open-source library for provable inference, with its protocol formalized in Lean, drew fast technical framing from the group. [tg:tawg:6375]

## 🤝 **What moved**

### proving stack

_The proving work moved from planned hardening into a concrete, reviewable change._

- Jimmy Shi **proposed** a refactor that pairs soundness hardening with a performance overhaul of the proving stack, giving reviewers one surface for both security and speed work on the infrastructure behind verifiable inference. [zkIE PR #47](https://github.com/trustless-ai/zkIE/pull/47)

### ERC-8183

_The evaluation-record conversation sharpened around what silence and explicit gaps actually mean._

- achemperety **isolated** the case where a check that cannot run leaves no record at all and asked what that silence should mean for anyone reading an agent's history, a gap that becomes load-bearing once agentic commerce leans on these logs. [ERC-8183 post 456](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8183-agentic-commerce/27902/456)

- nicholasparker **closed** the loop by noting that a dedicated record for unrun checks only helps if the evaluator actually submits it, surfacing the incentive question that separates a spec field from a dependable audit trail. [ERC-8183 post 457](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8183-agentic-commerce/27902/457)

### research

_A shared paper turned into shared context._

- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **shared** a FlashProve paper on an open-source library for provable inference, putting a concrete reference design in front of the group's own verification work. [tg:tawg:6373]

- Merlini (@gobross) **framed** it as a strong result, pointing to work from Chiesa and Anthropic on a succinct inference argument for a real 400B mixture-of-experts model with the protocol proved in Lean, which turns a link into a benchmark for how far the group's approach can reach. [tg:tawg:6375]

### daily bot

_The Daily's own feedback loop moved toward self-correction._

- Jimmy Shi **proposed** a fix that makes citation rejections actionable and self-healing, so a rejected Daily can correct itself instead of stalling, which keeps the group's shared record of progress flowing with less manual intervention. [Daily bot PR #15](https://github.com/trustless-ai/tawg-daily-contribution/pull/15)

### onboarding

_A new arrival got a real welcome._

- Merlini (@gobross) **greeted** the group's newest member and pointed them at the bot's intro as an easy entry point, lowering the friction for a newcomer to find their footing. [tg:tawg:6360]

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **welcomed** them with a warm personal hello, turning a routine join into a real introduction that makes people likelier to stay engaged. [tg:tawg:6369]

- 𝐆𝐄𝐄𝐊𓃵 (@superman_i4g) **replied** with thanks and clear enthusiasm, closing the welcome loop and signalling an engaged new participant for the group. [tg:tawg:6370]

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**

- What a silent gap in evaluation records should mean for downstream readers of an agent's history, and whether the spec text can carry that answer instead of thread replies.
- Whether the Lean-formalized inference argument behind the FlashProve work suggests techniques the group's own proving stack could adopt.
- How the Daily should decide when a citation rejection is recoverable feedback versus a genuine stop.

### ✅ **TODOs**

- Review the proving refactor for soundness gaps before relying on the performance numbers attached to it.
- Settle whether ERC-8183 should require an explicit unrun-check record or leave submission to the evaluator's discretion.
- Give the newest member a small concrete task so the welcome converts into a contribution.

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** A paper landed in the chat and was picked up soon after, decoded into plain terms, and tied back to the group's own work, a tidy relay from curiosity to shared understanding.
>
> Keep that habit going: toss ideas into the room and trust someone to catch them, turn them over, and send them back sharper. 🧩
